Calmer rose for long reading sessions.

host.note: Every role listed in the observed versions is set, so nothing falls through to a dark-ansi slot. Unknown tokens are ignored by Claude Code, so a role a newer version drops is harmless.

autoAccept.why: Accept-edits mode skips review: a caution state.

autoAcceptShimmer.why: Accept-edits shimmer (2.1.281 only); flat, as warningShimmer.

background.why: Background-task labels are a text accent, one rung above body text.

bashBorder.why: The shell-mode input still holds focus: the active border. The `!` marker, not a second border colour, carries the mode (see deviations).

bashMessageBackgroundColor.why: Shell entries on the default surface, distinct from your messages.

blue_FOR_SUBAGENTS_ONLY.why: Subagent names are text; seven distinct text roles for eight names, no hue outside status roles (D-001).

briefLabelClaude.why: Claude's label takes the brand accent.

briefLabelYou.why: Your label, one rung above body text.

chromeYellow.why: A product label; no yellow outside status roles (D-001).

claude.why: The brand accent and assistant label are emphasis, not links.

claudeBlueShimmer_FOR_SYSTEM_SPINNER.why: Shimmer step of the system spinner.

claudeBlue_FOR_SYSTEM_SPINNER.why: The system spinner is secondary activity.

clawd_background.why: The mascot sits on the terminal background.

clawd_body.why: The mascot is drawn in the brand accent.

composerSidebarBackground.why: The fullscreen sidebar is window chrome.

cyan_FOR_SUBAGENTS_ONLY.why: Subagent names are text; the text roles give seven distinct readable values for eight names, so cyan shares pink's (see deviations).

diffAddedDimmed.why: A rejected edit is inert: the disabled background.

diffAddedWord.why: j3w1 marks word-level changes with an underline in the emphasis colour; Claude can only paint a background, and the emphasis colour fails text contrast as a fill, so the word keeps the line tint (see deviations).

diffRemovedDimmed.why: A rejected edit is inert: the disabled background.

fastModeShimmer.why: Shimmer step of the fast-mode accent.

green_FOR_SUBAGENTS_ONLY.why: Subagent names are text; seven distinct text roles for eight names, no hue outside status roles (D-001).

ide.why: The IDE connection indicator is secondary status text.

inactive.why: Secondary text: hints, timestamps and disabled items take the muted rung of the text ladder.

inactiveShimmer.why: The lighter step of the inactive shimmer is the next rung up.

inverseText.why: Text on status fills; the badge on-fill rule for warning, success and info.

memoryBackgroundColor.why: Memory entries on the overlay surface.

merged.why: A merged pull request is an informational end state; there is no purple (D-001).

orange_FOR_SUBAGENTS_ONLY.why: Subagent names are text; seven distinct text roles for eight names, no hue outside status roles (D-001).

permission.why: Permission prompts and pickers are floating layers: the overlay border (use-and-report, D-008).

permissionShimmer.why: Shimmer step of the permission accent.

pink_FOR_SUBAGENTS_ONLY.why: Subagent names are text; seven distinct text roles for eight names, no hue outside status roles (D-001).

planMode.why: Plan mode is an informational state (status.info).

professionalBlue.why: Secondary informational text; no blue outside status roles (D-001).

promptBorder.why: The input box always holds focus while you type: the active border.

promptBorderShimmer.why: Shimmer step of the input border.

rate_limit_empty.why: The unfilled track is chart grid.

rate_limit_fill.why: A single-series meter uses the approved red chart role (spec/components/chart.md).

red_FOR_SUBAGENTS_ONLY.why: Subagent names are text; seven distinct text roles for eight names, no hue outside status roles (D-001).

remember.why: Memory and CLAUDE.md indicators read as a label, one rung above body text.

selectionBg.why: Mouse selection keeps each span's own colour (Claude has no selection-text token), which is the editor-selection case: text stays readable on it (spec/foundations.md, Code and terminal).

skill.why: Skill labels are a text accent.

text.why: Default foreground; dark-ansi uses slot 15, which measures 4.45:1.

userMessageBackground.why: Your messages sit on the selected-row red, a clearly visible band (6.24:1 for the rose text); chosen by the owner over the fainter raised surface.

userMessageBackgroundHover.why: Hover and expanded rows step up to the strong hover fill (5.71:1).

warning.why: Status warning (D-001); Claude also uses it for the auto-mode indicator.

deviations.applied: heritage ANSI slots chosen by Claude Code
deviations.reason: Claude Code colours highlighted code from fixed ANSI slots that a theme cannot override; the terminal spec lets programs choose slot semantics.
Claude Code draws OSC 8 links in bright blue (slot 12) regardless of theme.

deviations.applied: ANSI slots 10 and 9 and the preview slots
deviations.reason: Hard-coded to ANSI slots in Claude Code.
Claude Code can only paint word changes as a background; the emphasis colours fail text contrast as fills.
Claude Code colours the selected item's text only; it has no selection-fill token for pickers.

deviations.specValue: a distinct border for a distinct input mode
deviations.reason: j3w1 defines one focused-input border; the `!` prompt marker carries the mode.
Claude Code draws inline code in its permission colour, which the kit maps to the overlay border for dialogs.

deviations.applied: seven distinct text roles; cyan shares pink's value
deviations.reason: j3w1 has no categorical text palette and permits no hue outside status roles (D-001). Cyan and pink share one role (text.bright); two further pairs are close: orange text.accent / red text.accent-strong, purple text.muted / blue text.subtle.

deviations.applied: color.code.selection-bg; spans keep their own colour
deviations.reason: Claude Code has a selection background token only, so spans keep their own colour on color.code.selection-bg: text.default 7.02:1 and text.muted 4.71:1 stay above 4.5:1, while text.subtle (4.13:1), text.accent-strong and status.danger.text (4.38:1), and text.accent and border.overlay (3.81:1) fall below it inside the selection, as spec/foundations.md accepts for syntax roles in an editor selection.

deviations.target: status, diff signs, brand and status line
deviations.reason: Codex names these colours by ANSI slot; a theme cannot remap them, and the terminal spec lets programs choose slot semantics.

deviations.applied: the terminal background blended toward white by Codex
deviations.reason: Codex computes these fills from the terminal background; no setting reaches them.

deviations.specValue: comments italic; links, invalid text underlined; deprecated text line-through
deviations.applied: plain text in the role colour
deviations.reason: Codex renders only bold from a tmTheme (codex-rs/tui/src/render/highlight.rs skips italic and underline).
Codex paints no code background, line highlight, selection or gutter from a tmTheme; it uses only scope foregrounds and the inserted/deleted backgrounds.
Codex reads backgrounds only for markup.inserted and markup.deleted.

deviations.specValue: row text color.text.default with an emphasis underline
deviations.applied: syntax colours on the line tint
deviations.reason: Codex keeps syntax colours inside diff lines and draws no underlines; the tmTheme sets only the line backgrounds. On those tints code.syntax.heading, code.syntax.invalid and the codex.accent (text.accent) measure 4.23:1 on diff.added.bg and 4.24:1 on diff.removed.bg, below 4.5:1; every other syntax role measures 4.59:1 or more. text.accent is also used here outside its documented canvas-and-surface scope.

host.note: Codex opts in to the hued syntax roles (D-030): green strings; amber numbers, constants, functions, attributes and escapes; blue types and properties; bright-rose operators. Keywords, tags, comments, variables and punctuation keep code.syntax.
